children: The Mexican government's 2027 budget proposal makes "realistic assumptions" about growth and public finances while capturing "the limits of fiscal consolidation amidst a low-growth environment," Barclays analysts say in a note. The Finance Ministry assumes GDP growth of 2% next year, up from 1.5% in 2026. The public sector deficit is expected to narrow to 3.9% of GDP from 4.1% this year. Public sector debt is projected to rise to 55% of GDP from 54% at the end of 2026. "Mexico is likely to keep its investment grade status in the coming years given the Mexican economy is now growing above 1%--one of the rating agency warning thresholds--and is projected to do so (even more) in the next few years," Barclays says. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
